It is weighed here as a real onset in its own right, not folded into or discounted against the vision that follows. The messenger formula at 5:5, כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.5.5), opens the act's own interpretation rather than a competing unit (no refrain close intervenes between the hair-sign and its meaning). The oath at 5:11, חַי אָ֗נִי ('as I live'), with the utterance signature נְאֻם֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ (oshb:Ezek.5.11) attached mid-verse, marks an emphatic sub-onset of the verdict paragraph, not a unit boundary. The formula 'I, Yahweh, have spoken' recurs three times, at 5:13 (אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה דִּבַּ֨רְתִּי֙ (oshb:Ezek.5.13)), 5:15 (אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי (oshb:Ezek.5.15)) and 5:17 (אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי (oshb:Ezek.5.17)); the first two are paragraph-final rather than unit-final because no fresh onset device follows either (5:14 continues 'moreover I will make you a desolation' with no messenger formula or word-event reopening the address). Close: 5:17, with a pe recorded after it, before 6:1 opens with a fresh strict word-event. The verdict continues in two further 'therefore' messenger formulae addressing the same party: 5:7, לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣י (oshb:Ezek.5.7) (2mp, 'therefore the Lord Yahweh says'), and 5:8, לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י (oshb:Ezek.5.8) (2fs, 'therefore the Lord Yahweh says') — both verdict paragraphs inside the same interpretation, addressing Jerusalem and the people in her as one party, with no refrain standing before either (the samekh after 5:6, 5:7 and 5:9 are disclosed as intra-row texture, not unit-cutting seams). The verdict is bound to the sign-act itself by a byte-identical clause: 5:12 closes with the same words that close 5:2, וְחֶ֖רֶב אָרִ֥יק אַחֲרֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Ezek.5.2; oshb:Ezek.5.12) ('and I will draw a sword after them', sweep: 3 verses book-wide, the third at 12:14).
